The BRIC program was a classic example of pre-disaster waste—dumping millions into projects with zero accountability. H.R. 316’s Natural Disaster Recovery Program prioritizes post-disaster rebuilding with strict fiscal controls, unlike BRIC’s slush fund approach. Richmond’s plant failed because decades of mismanagement went unaddressed while bureaucrats chased grant dollars.

The $12M cancellation isn’t about denying upgrades—it’s about redirecting funds to projects that meet actual disaster recovery metrics under Section 431’s unmet needs framework.

If localities want federal cash, they should prove necessity through the Stafford Act’s updated accountability protocols, not political earmarks.

The empathy gap closes with practical access, not political theater. Cut the waste, fund the mission.
